## What it means for Ward

- Claude Code alone finds almost every planted issue: 21.7 of 23 on
  average, never fewer than 21. Its misses are an absence (EA-23, no
  account deletion) and a known-vulnerable Gson version (EA-19).
- Its weak spot is the clean twin: 1 to 3 false alarms per run, mostly
  decoys. Every run of every arm flagged EA-D7 (backup on, with rules).
- The checklist skill was used in 6 of 6 runs and changed nothing
  measurable. OWASP's plugin was never used (0 of 6): its skill didn't
  trigger on "is it ready to publish?", so that arm is "alone" again.
- ADR 0001's pre-registered bar is not triggered, but only because of
  twin false alarms. On recall alone it is met (21.7 against 21).
- For Ward: recall on textbook issues isn't where it can win. What's
  left: fewer false alarms, real citations, privacy and Play rules, and
  harder or held-out cases. A skill that never triggers adds nothing.

## About these runs

- 3 trials × 3 arms × 2 apps, interleaved by trial, all on 2026-11-22.
  Same model, prompt, schema, tools (Read, Grep, Glob, Skill) and
  isolation in every arm; only the plugin differs.
- Hand grades: proposed by Claude, confirmed by Karlo (`proposed` and
  `label` in each `grades.json`).
- `cc-plugin-easel`, a built-in Claude Code plugin, loaded in 2 of 18
  runs (checklist-planted-t1, owasp-planted-t3). Tools and skills were
  the same as in the other runs.
- Each `meta.json` records repo commit 0c0d684, but the runner, setups
  and checklist plugin were not committed yet; they are in the commit
  that adds these results.
